73460105_a5d177e9.text: The intergeniculate leaflet (IGL) of the thalamus is a part of the circadian timing system that is strongly connected with the SCN, the master biological clock. This nucleus is located between the dorsal and ventral parts of the lateral geniculate nucleus. The neuronal network of the IGL mainly consists of the γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA)ergic neurons that co-expressed two distinct neuropeptides: enkephalin (ENK) or neuropeptide Y (NPY; (Moore et al., 1994). The characteristic feature of enkephalinergic neurons is the generation of infra-slow oscillations (ISO) in vivo. Moreover, this subpopulation of the IGL neurons is responsible for connecting IGLs in both hemispheres to each other (for review see: (Lewandowski et al., 2000). The second subpopulation of the IGL neurons (NPY-positive cells) connects the IGL with the SCN (Glass et al., 2010)Harrington, 1997;Moore & Card, 1994). Both IGL subpopulations are distinguished based on their electrophysiological properties.
